items.title: McDonald's Japan data breach exposes customer location information

ai.summary: McDonald's Japan disclosed a breach in which attackers accessed a database holding sensitive data of users of its official smartphone app, including location information.

items.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation

ai.summary: Broadcom patched 23 VMware flaws, including critical CVE-2026-123903, a 9.8-rated authentication bypass in vCenter's directory service that follows zero-day exploitation.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

ai.summary: CISA added two actively exploited flaws, in Project MONAI Label and N-able Mail Assure, to its KEV catalog. The listing obliges US federal civilian agencies to patch them under a new directive.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning

ai.summary: Attackers are exploiting a patched critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw (CVE-2026-84869) to target MSP servers, letting guests push and run payloads on technicians' machines.

items.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and a Whole Lot of Shell Trouble

ai.summary: Weekly roundup of security stories, including a VMware zero-day and several shell-related flaws, showing how stolen keys, trusted messages and routine updates let attackers gain access.

items.title: Okta Links ShinyHunters-Associated Vishing Group to New INCEPTION Data Leak Site

ai.summary: Okta says a vishing cluster linked to ShinyHunters may have rebranded as INCEPTION and launched a new data leak site, using phone-based social engineering to steal credentials and approvals.

items.title: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace says third-party breach leaked donation info

ai.summary: Some donors to the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace had their information exposed after a cyberattack on third-party vendor Soapbox Engage.

items.title: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach

ai.summary: The European Commission confirmed attackers breached its EU Academy online learning platform and stole personal data of an undisclosed number of users.

items.title: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million

ai.summary: Attackers breached the internal network of South Korea's state power utility KEPCO and accessed two systems holding customer, employee, and contractor data. About 1.5 million people are affected.

items.title: LaLiga hacked: Spain’s top football league confirms theft of fans’ personal data

ai.summary: Spain's LaLiga football league said hackers stole fans' personal data in a cyberattack that also affected its digital services and several Spanish clubs.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching

ai.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime that lets AI agents create eBPF controls to block exploits, giving defenders time to patch without downtime.

items.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login

ai.summary: A SQL injection flaw in WHMCS billing software, used by many web hosts, lets unauthenticated attackers retrieve customer records and admin password hashes. The vendor has released a fix.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes Azure API Management Classic Flaw as Actor Targets Customer Secrets

ai.summary: Norway's NSM reported an Azure API Management flaw affecting several Norwegian businesses, including energy firms Equinor and Skagerak Energi. An unknown actor was seeking access tokens and secrets.

items.title: Schneider Electric EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software

ai.summary: Schneider Electric disclosed memory corruption and buffer overflow flaws in its EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software, which local attackers could exploit to run arbitrary code. Remediations are provided.

items.title: Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series

ai.summary: Danfoss disclosed a critical stack-based buffer overflow in its AK-SM 8xxA controllers, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to run code with webserver privileges. The product is deployed worldwide.

items.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software

ai.summary: AutomationDirect disclosed a heap-based buffer overflow in its C-More EA9 programming software. Opening a malicious file could crash it or allow code execution in critical manufacturing, energy and water sectors.

items.title: 2027 SOC Budget Reset: 5 Priorities to Cut Costs and Reduce Cyber Risk

ai.summary: A vendor article argues SOC teams could recover about 450 analyst hours per 1,000 alerts by speeding up threat analysis and IOC research, reducing costs from manual investigations and escalations.

items.title: Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity

ai.summary: Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw showed a .NET Framework file-loading quirk that let local attackers run untrusted code past Windows code integrity protections and bypass Oracle VirtualBox hardening, tracked as CVE-2026-87268.

items.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap

ai.summary: Attackers who hijacked the open-source scanner Trivy planted malicious code disguised as GitHub's official checkout tool, bypassing SHA pinning defenses used against supply chain attacks.

items.title: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits

ai.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source Linux tool that applies temporary runtime protections to block exploits on unpatched systems without restarting services.

items.title: UK cyber agency seeing ‘marked rise’ in AI-driven attacks

ai.summary: The UK National Cyber Security Centre reports a marked rise since September in cyberattacks assisted by artificial intelligence, which it says increases attackers' speed, scale and persistence.

items.title: CISA warns of exploited N-able bug as company restores email platform

ai.summary: CISA ordered US government departments to patch an exploited N-able flaw in an email security platform by Thanksgiving, while the vendor restores the affected platform.

items.title: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era

ai.summary: Vendor RapidFort argues that AI-driven development complicates software supply chains and proposes runtime visibility, container hardening and automated remediation to cut vulnerability noise.

items.title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits

ai.summary: Law enforcement from 11 countries disrupted 57 illegal streaming services running hundreds of websites that drew over 7.3 million visits each year.

items.title: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations

ai.summary: Threat actors exploited several vulnerabilities to compromise about two dozen Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign affecting 22 organizations.

items.title: ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof

ai.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang says it has returned with a new data leak site after recent arrests of alleged members, using old PGP keys as proof.

items.title: AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks Trigger Unauthorized Payments at Indian Banks and Fintech Firms

ai.summary: CERT-In warned that AI-assisted attacks on Indian ICT assets have caused unauthorized financial transactions at banks, financial services firms and technology providers.

items.title: Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices

ai.summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service to infect some customer travel routers and KVM devices with malware. The company fixed the flaw and blocked the attacker's access.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE

ai.summary: A critical flaw (CVE-2026-131914) in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf ASP.NET library is being exploited in the wild to allow unauthenticated code execution. Users are told to stop using it.

items.title: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans

ai.summary: A Peruvian call center operator received an eight-year prison sentence for running a government-impersonation scam that defrauded over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents of millions.

items.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions

ai.summary: A critical code injection flaw (CVE-2026-134814) in binary-parser versions before 2.3.1 lets an attacker controlling parser definitions execute arbitrary code.

items.title: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops

ai.summary: Microsoft is working on a fix for a long-running Windows 11 issue causing significant audio quality drops for Bluetooth headphone users.

items.title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap

ai.summary: Discusses how AI agents spanning several platforms leave security gaps because no single vendor can monitor them, and how organisations can manage agent identities, permissions and accountability.

items.title: GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards

ai.summary: A cyberattack disrupted operations at B2B top-up provider GlobeTopper, costing an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue, while the attacker redeemed $70,000 in digital gift cards.

items.title: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access

ai.summary: China-aligned Webworm is suspected of using a modified SoftEther VPN Bridge that hides from security tools and disguises itself as network monitoring software to maintain covert remote access.

items.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data

ai.summary: Spain's top men's football league LaLiga disclosed a breach exposing personal data of users of its services and those of some affiliated clubs.

items.title: Microsoft Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials

ai.summary: Microsoft warns that a flaw in Azure API Management Classic tiers was exploited to steal stored API credentials, with Norwegian authorities linking it to attacks on energy companies.

items.title: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets

ai.summary: OpenRouter removed three AI providers from its platform after they were found to have breached their data-handling policies and exposed sensitive information.

items.title: Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps

ai.summary: A patched Ghostscript flaw lets a crafted file escape its sandbox and run commands on servers that process uploads, according to researchers at pwn.ai.

ai.summary: Attackers secretly stole customer prompts from three AI inference providers for months. The providers were unaware until Dragos alerted them. OpenRouter dropped the three providers from its gateway.

groups.name: thegentlemen
groups.about: The Gentlemen is a ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in July–August 2025 and quickly claimed over 320 victims in 17+ countries. It offers affiliates a 90% revenue share and uses a Go-based locker against Windows, Linux, NAS, and BSD. A 2026 compromised C2 server revealed over 1,570 linked victims.

groups.name: qilin
groups.about: Qilin ransomware was first observed in July 2022. It is written in Golang and offers multiple encryption modes that the operator controls. The group uses double extortion, demanding payment for a decryptor and for not releasing stolen data.

groups.name: incransom
groups.about: INC Ransom is a prolific ransomware-as-a-service operation active since July 2023. It targets healthcare, government, education, and manufacturing in North America and Europe, with no sector excluded. It posted over 200 victims in 2025 alone.

groups.name: safepay
groups.about: SafePay emerged in September 2024 and grew rapidly while rejecting the RaaS model, running all operations in-house. It claimed over 300 victims worldwide by mid-2025. An early high-profile attack on UK telematics firm Microlise reportedly stole 1.2 TB of data.

groups.name: akira
groups.about: Akira reportedly emerged in March 2023 and has been speculated to have ties to the former Conti group. Its affiliates reportedly also work with Snatch and BlackByte. The first version was written in C++ and later versions in Rust. Initial access has involved brute-force attacks on Cisco VPNs and exploitation of two CVEs.

groups.name: silentransomgroup
groups.about: Silentransomgroup is described in the notes as a former Conti team, also tracked as Chatty Spider and UNC3753. The notes give no further details on its operations or targets.

groups.name: rhysida
groups.about: Rhysida is a ransomware-as-a-service group that emerged in May 2023. It uses phishing and Cobalt Strike to breach networks and deploy its payload. It threatens to publish stolen data, leaves PDF notes, and accepts Bitcoin. The notes say the ransomware is still in early development.

groups.name: medusalocker
groups.about: The notes describe Medusa as a DDoS bot written in .NET 2.0, not a ransomware group. Its current command-and-control uses HTTP, while its predecessor used IRC. The notes do not describe ransomware activity, so this entry may be mislabeled.

groups.name: everest
groups.about: Everest collects and analyzes information about its victims, focusing on customer privacy, financial data, databases, and credit card information. It leaks stolen data on the darknet. It threatens to leak data and keep victims' files if they do not make contact.

groups.name: aurora
groups.about: Aurora is ransomware associated with a multi-purpose Go-based malware in use since mid-2022. Multiple criminal teams distribute it, and it is also sold on underground forums as an infostealer and botnet under the same name.

groups.name: braincipher
groups.about: Brain Cipher emerged in July 2024 with both Windows and Linux variants. It reportedly uses a leaked LockBit Black build and is suspected of exploiting CVE-2023-28252. Demands start at $150,000 and are paid in Monero. In 2025 it moved its negotiation portal to a new server.

groups.name: lockbit5
groups.about: LockBit 5.0, also called ChuongDong, emerged in September 2025 after the February 2024 law enforcement takedown of LockBit. It introduced cross-platform payloads targeting Windows, Linux, and VMware ESXi. It continues the RaaS affiliate model of its predecessors.

groups.name: metaencryptor
groups.about: Ransomware group first observed in mid-2023. Targets medium-to-large enterprises in legal, technology, logistics, manufacturing, and finance, mainly in the UK, Europe, and Southeast Asia. Uses AES-256 and RSA-2048 encryption with double extortion.

groups.name: payload
groups.about: Payload emerged in early 2026 and uses Babuk-derived source code to attack Windows and ESXi systems with double extortion. It targets healthcare, energy, real estate, and agriculture. It claimed 12 victims across seven countries within hours of launching its leak site.

groups.name: everstake
groups.about: The notes say this group is not affiliated with Everstake, Inc., a legitimate blockchain infrastructure company. They suggest the group may be misusing that company's name. The notes give no details on when it appeared, how it operates, or who it targets.

groups.name: genesis
groups.about: Emerging ransomware group first observed in late 2025. Targets small and mid-sized US organizations in healthcare, retail, finance, legal, and manufacturing. Uses double extortion, emphasizing data theft and public leaking of stolen information.

"That's not a browser. That's a desktop app."

Okay, great. So the same sensitive data needs one security tool in Chrome and another in Slack? One for Edge and another for WhatsApp?

Same data. Same actions. Same risks.

Are we sure it needs a different security stack?

93% of the top 200 applications run on browser-based surfaces, embed a browser, or embed AI. The line between "browser security" and "desktop security" is getting harder to defend.

Different wrapper. Same web session underneath.

That’s why session security focuses on what users actually do: what they paste, upload, download, and send across the browsers, AI tools, and other apps where they work.

Don't agree? Here's the full case. See what you think after reading it: https://t.co/VupxsUHuwW

After Hugging Face there was this silly discourse about how you can't do anything against zero-day exploits.

Assume you have one of those enterprise gateway/firewall appliances that have zero-days found in their web management interfaces every other week.

For arguments sake, I'm going to simply accept that you can't take the management interface offline. You can't configure it to be accessible only from the local network. It has to be accessible to anyone connecting from anywhere.

The overwhelming majority of threat actors (including state-sponsored ones) tend to be overly reliant on internet scanning. They use services like Shodan/Censys, which scan every IPv4 address, then create indexes listing all the devices they find.

Threat actors then come along, use a search query to export a list of "<insert appliance type> by <insert vendor>", then either mass-exploit them, or pick and choose the devices belonging to organizations they're interested in.

One option: Create a subdomain, ideally something not easily guessable like "firewall-​a4f8d5.​yourcompany​.com". 

Sign up for a proxy/CDN provider like Cloudflare or similar. Configure the provider to forward traffic designated for that domain to the public IP address of your appliance, then enable revere proxy mode.

Now, go into your firewall and set up a rule to block all access to the management interface from IPs not belonging to Cloudflare. Either with an CIDR or ASN allow list.

Your device now doesn't show up in any internet scans at all, including those provided by Shodan or Censys, and the device is not directly accessible via IP address. But it is still accessible to anyone with the domain.

You've now reduced your blast radius from "every zero-day (or n-day if you don't patch immediately) is rocking my device" to "99.9% of exploitation attempts don't even see it", all without sacrificing availability.

Highly targeted attacker may go to the extra effort of figuring out the subdomain you use, and try to exploit the devices through the reverse proxy. But the way reverse proxies work breaks a lot of exploits, and Web Application Firewalls add a layer of additional protection.

Techniques like this work for most web-based appliances (which tend to get hit a lot as the result of internet scans). And there are plenty of simple things you can do for other software/devices which massively reduces your attack surface. Just one extra layer between the attacker and the target works wonders.

The whole "zero-day exploits are unstoppable" attitude is extremely defeatists, and also extremely wrong. Ask your friendly neighborhood blue teamer or threat intelligence professional for attack surface reduction advice.

digest.overview: Critical VMware vCenter and ESX flaws, actively exploited SAP and other vulnerabilities, a Check Point server compromise, and ShinyHunters-linked extortion dominate today's defender-relevant reporting.

themes.title: Critical VMware vCenter and ESX flaws patched
themes.summary: The Hacker News reports a new vCenter authentication bypass (CVSS 9.8) that lets network-adjacent attackers skip authentication, days after a similar zero-day was exploited in attacks. SecurityWeek separately reports VMware patched critical ESX and vCenter vulnerabilities. Both sources point to urgent patching of virtualization management systems.

themes.title: Actively exploited SAP, Azure and PHP flaws
themes.summary: Onapsis confirms attacks exploiting an SAP NetWeaver flaw (CVSS 6.5) that could enable remote code execution, with no public exploit available. watchTowr observed in-the-wild exploitation of an RCE in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library, with probes triggering web redirects. BleepingComputer reports an Azure flaw exploited to steal customers' API credentials.

themes.title: ShinyHunters-linked Inception extortion and voice phishing
themes.summary: Okta links an active voice phishing group to a new data leak site named Inception, tied to ShinyHunters, involving account takeovers, data theft and extortion. Unit42 reports a related campaign using legal-themed domains, some affiliated with Inception. BleepingComputer reports ShinyHunters claims to be back after arrests, though its control of the group is unverified.

themes.title: Data breaches at KEPCO, European Commission and LaLiga
themes.summary: KEPCO confirmed a data breach affecting 1.5 million people, reported by both SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer. The European Commission confirmed data theft in an EU Academy breach, and LaLiga said hackers stole fans' personal information. These are notification-level breach reports with no technical details on initial access.

themes.title: Check Point security management servers compromised
themes.summary: BleepingComputer reports hackers compromised Check Point servers in 22 organizations. SecurityWeek describes the same incident as an AI-assisted campaign targeting Check Point Security Management Servers. Both sources agree on the compromise, but the posts do not name a CVE.

points.title: BerriAI LiteLLM unprotected alternate channel flaw
points.why: Confirmed exploited and added within the last week, with a high likelihood of further exploitation within 30 days.
